BootstrapToken.name: X-WorkMesh-Bootstrap-Token
BootstrapToken.description: One-time deployment bootstrap credential. It is required for Workspace installation and is not a human or Agent session.

AgentSessionToken.description: Short-lived agent session token; revocation is checked server-side.

AgentConnectionInstallationToken.name: X-WorkMesh-Installation-Token
AgentConnectionInstallationToken.description: Agent Connection credential used only for Coordination MCP and current-identity requests. It is distinct from pairing codes and from Bearer installation-target credentials.

AgentInstallationToken.description: Installation-scoped bearer credential used by installation_target operations, including token exchange, refresh, and exact-target handoff actions. It cannot perform ordinary session work.

GitHubWebhookSignature.name: X-Hub-Signature-256
GitHubWebhookSignature.description: GitHub HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body. X-GitHub-Delivery and X-GitHub-Event are also required and the server enforces its replay and delivery rules.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Versioned, signed, opaque continuation cursor. It is bound to the route, workspace, actor, effective filters, and sort tuple; clients must not decode or modify it.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of authorized items returned in this page.

Limit100.name: limit
Limit100.description: Maximum number of authorized control-plane digests returned for the selected collection.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Identifies one logical mutation attempt. Authentication and secret-bearing session mutations retain an encrypted replay for 15 minutes and protect key conflicts for 24 hours. A different operation, canonical request, or client context returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; an exact retry after the replay window returns IDEMPOTENCY_REPLAY_EXPIRED and must use a new key.

GuidanceIfMatch.name: If-Match
GuidanceIfMatch.description: Guidance uses revision-0 as the explicit unpublished resource version.

CorrelationId.name: X-Correlation-Id
CorrelationId.description: Optional caller trace value. Use only ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen; credential-looking prefixes are rejected. Authorization denial audit uses a separate server-generated request id.

CursorQuery.name: cursor
CursorQuery.description: Canonical decimal PostgreSQL domain-event cursor; distinct from opaque collection and A2A cursors

RunSequenceCursor.name: cursor

credential_fingerprint_prefix.description: First 12 characters of the active credential fingerprint; never the credential itself.

connect_url.description: URL the Human pastes to the Agent. The plaintext wmp_ pairing code travels in the URL fragment so it never reaches proxy access logs and is visibly distinct from a wmi_ Installation Token. The pattern enforces: https origin, no userinfo (https://user:pass@host is rejected), host with no @, the exact /connect path, and an exact wmp_ fragment. The server-side Zod superRefine adds a defense-in-depth check that no credential-leak patterns (pairing_code, code, secret, token, access_token) appear in the query or path, plus a URL parser check that rejects userinfo.

pairingCode.description: Plaintext wmp_ pairing code carried in the URL fragment; sent verbatim by the Agent. It is single-use and must never be configured as an MCP Installation Token.

installation_token.description: Plaintext wmi_ Installation Token returned exactly once per pairing code. It is deliberately distinguishable from the wmp_ pairing code. The server stores only its fingerprint; clients must verify SHA-256(installation_token)[0:12] equals connection.credential_fingerprint_prefix before persisting it. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key returns the exact same body (see idempotency_replay). Note: this is a response field, not an input field; the input-only flag is not set because strict client generators would strip the field and break first redeem and Idempotency-Key replay.

header.description: Custom header (not Authorization) to keep the token out of generic Bearer auth logs.

idempotency_replay.description: Server promise that replays with the same Idempotency-Key, before replayable_until, return the exact same response body. Implements the plan section 'Pairing and Connection Security' (public interface and security model): success responses are safely replayable via the existing encrypted authentication idempotency mechanism.

connect_url.description: New connect URL with the new wmp_ pairing code in the fragment. The old URL stays valid until overlap_until. Same fragment-only contract as AgentConnectionCreateResponse; no userinfo, no path/query credentials.

overlap_until.description: Real deadline after which the worker auto-invalidates the old fingerprint. The old Installation Token is accepted until this timestamp; afterwards only the new one is valid. There is no auto-revoke on the new redeem's success.

AgentWellKnownResponse.description: Public discovery manifest served from /.well-known/workmesh-agent. Wire format is camelCase because clients read it before any WorkMesh session exists. Never includes secret material.

CoordinationSession.description: Coordination Session is a Team-scope session. delegation_scope is locked to 'team' so the public contract does not weaken Team isolation. The Zod schema uses z.literal('team') with the same intent. granted_capabilities is uniqueItems:true and cross-validated against connection.granted_capabilities inside AgentConnectionIdentity (see AgentConnectionIdentity allOf for the 17 + 17 + 17 subset/equality blocks).

AgentConnectionIdentity.description: The per-request identity a Coordination MCP request resolves to. Returned by get_current_identity and embedded in every successful MCP response envelope. Cross-field invariants (also enforced in Zod via superRefine for non-OpenAPI clients): (1) coordination_session.granted_capabilities is a subset of connection.granted_capabilities; (2) identity.granted_capabilities equals coordination_session.granted_capabilities; (3) all three capability arrays are unique. The 17 + 17 + 17 if/then/else blocks in allOf are the OpenAPI enforcement of these rules (JSON Schema 2020-12 has no subset operator). CROSS-IDENTITY ID BINDING (8 equalities; Zod superRefine-only because JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot compare two dynamic values): (d.1) coordination_session.connection_id === connection.id; (d.2) coordination_session.team_id === connection.team_id; (d.3) coordination_session.team_id === identity.team_id; (d.4) coordination_session.principal_human_actor_id === connection.principal_human_actor_id; (d.5) coordination_session.principal_human_actor_id === identity.principal_human_actor_id; (d.6) identity.agent_actor_id === connection.agent_actor_id; (d.7) identity.team_id === connection.team_id; (d.8) identity.principal_human_actor_id === connection.principal_human_actor_id.

Different or live assignments remain conflicts. Eligibility is bound to the exact Connection Team, principal human, Agent actor, approved capabilities, and active Coordination Session. The exchange token is returned only through the encrypted authentication-idempotency envelope; MCP adapters exchange it internally and never expose it to the model.
